problems.title: Reflect across an angle bisector
problems.question: In ABC, lines through A,C perpendicular to the B-bisector meet BC,AB at K,M. BM=9 and KC=2. Which listed value can equal AB?
problems.idea: Reflection across the bisector swaps the two side rays.
steps: The perpendicular joining A to its reflected point on BC gives K; similarly C reflects to M.
Thus KC=|BK−BC|=|AB−9|=2.
AB may be 7 or 11; only 7 is listed.
problems.answer: Listed value 7; the two possible lengths are 7 and 11.

problems.title: An angle between incircle contact points
problems.question: The incircle touches AB,BC,AC at K,M,N. Angle KNM is 37.5% less than B. Find KNM.
problems.idea: The contact radii enclose angle 180°−B.
steps: It also equals 0.625B. Thus 90°=1.125B, giving B=80°.
The desired angle is 0.625·80°.

problems.title: Clock hands at 3:12
problems.question: Find the smaller angle between clock hands at 3:12.
problems.idea: Include the hour hand’s movement after 3:00.
steps: The difference is 24°.

problems.title: A right triangle’s altitude controls its acute angles
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse 4.8 cm and altitude to it 1.2 cm. Find the difference of its acute angles.
problems.idea: Express the altitude in terms of one acute angle.
formulas: If c is the hypotenuse, h=c sinα cosα=(c/2)sin2α.
steps: The acute angles are 15° and 75°. Their difference is 60°.

problems.title: Maximize a reciprocal of a square plus one
problems.question: Find the maximum of 1/(x²+1)−1/3.
problems.idea: The denominator is at least 1.
steps: Equality holds at x=0. Subtract 1/3.

problems.title: An altitude and a base-angle bisector
problems.question: In isosceles MNK, MN=NK. Altitude MP and bisector KQ meet at O. If 5·angle MNK=2·angle POK, find MNK.
problems.idea: Use the right triangle KPO.
formulas: Let apex angle N=θ. The base angle K=(180°−θ)/2, so angle PKO=45°−θ/4.
steps: KPO is right at P, so POK=45°+θ/4.
The condition gives 5θ=90°+θ/2.

problems.title: One worker finishes first and then helps
problems.question: Two workers must each make the same number of parts. Worker 1 makes 3/8 of that number in 6 hours; worker 2 makes 1/8 in 3 hours. They start together, and the first helps the second after finishing. When are both jobs complete?
problems.idea: Both workers remain productive throughout, so combine their rates for the two equal jobs.
formulas: Rates=1/16 and 1/24 job per hour; combined rate=5/48.
steps: There are two jobs in total. Time=2/(5/48)=96/5 hours.
The first finishes at 16 hours; the second still has work, so this combined-rate model is valid.
96/5=19.2 hours=19 hours 12 minutes.

problems.title: Two intersection facts still do not fix a slope sign
problems.question: For f(x)=kx+b, I:its intersection with y=7 is in the first quadrant; II:its x-intercept is (199,0). Do these determine the sign of k?
problems.idea: Construct one positive-slope and one negative-slope example satisfying both.
formulas: With the given intercept, f(x)=k(x−199); the y=7 intersection has x=199+7/k.
steps: For k=1 this x is 206>0.
For k=−1 it is 192>0. Both intersections are in the first quadrant and both lines have x-intercept 199.
Thus even the two conditions together do not determine the sign.
problems.answer: The information is insufficient, even together.

problems.title: Cancel equal quadratic terms
problems.question: Solve (5x−9)²−(3x−2)²=(7−4x)²−(7+4x)²−8x(4−2x).
problems.idea: Expand both sides and cancel their x² terms.
steps: Thus 66x+77=0, giving x=−77/66.

problems.title: Four arcs made by an isosceles triangle
problems.question: The base AC of an isosceles triangle with apex angle 50° is a circle’s diameter. The two legs cut the circle into four arcs. Find the smallest arc.
problems.idea: Use the external-secant angle at the apex and symmetry.
formulas: The far arc AC is 180°; exterior apex angle=half(far arc−near arc).
steps: 50°=(180°−near arc)/2 gives the near arc 80°.
The other two arcs lie in the same semicircle and are equal by symmetry. Their total is 180°−80°=100°.
Each is 50°, and the fourth arc is 180°.

problems.title: Dilute a sugar syrup
problems.question: How much water must be added to 20 kg of 12% sugar syrup to make 10% syrup?
problems.idea: The sugar mass stays fixed.
steps: Add 24−20=4 kg of water.

problems.title: Factor common powers in a fraction
problems.question: Evaluate (6¹⁰−6⁹−6⁸)/(3¹¹+3⁹−3⁸).
problems.idea: Factor out 6⁸ from the numerator and 3⁸ from the denominator.
steps: Cancel 29 and simplify (6/3)⁸.

problems.title: A right angle from two tangent circles
problems.question: Two circles touch externally at M and have common tangent NK. Given MNK is 20° smaller than NKM, find NMK.
problems.idea: The angle at M is always right in this tangent configuration.
formulas: Let the common tangent at M meet NK at T. Tangent lengths give TN=TM=TK.
steps: T lies between N and K, so it is the midpoint of NK and TM=NK/2.
Thus M is on the circle with diameter NK, giving NMK=90°.
The other two angles are 35° and 55°, consistent with the 20° difference.

problems.title: Count coordinate pairs from polynomial roots
problems.question: A point (x₀,y₀) is marked for every root x₀ of x³+6x²−4x−24=0 and every root y₀ of y³+4y²+4y=0. How many distinct points?
problems.idea: Factor both polynomials and count distinct roots.
steps: There are three x-values −6,−2,2 and two y-values 0,−2.
Every x may pair with every y.

problems.title: Count distinct prime divisors after factoring
problems.question: For integer k>2019, how many distinct primes divide 4^{2k}·4+4^{2k}:4?
problems.idea: Factor the smaller power of 4.
steps: The only distinct prime divisors are 2 and 17.

problems.title: Add the lengths of two axis intercepts
problems.question: The line 4y−1=2(y+x−1) cuts the axes at A,B. Find OA+OB.
problems.idea: Simplify to slope-intercept form.
steps: The intercepts are (1/2,0) and (0,−1/2).
Their distances from the origin sum to 1.

problems.title: An inscribed angle from half an arc
problems.question: In the printed circle, AB=AC, arc AD=arc CD and angle BAC=40°. Find the marked angle ABD.
problems.idea: Equal chords AB,AC give equal arcs.
formulas: Arc BC=2·40°=80°; arcs AB and AC each equal (360°−80°)/2=140°.
steps: D bisects arc AC, so arc AD=70°.
The inscribed angle ABD is half arc AD.

problems.title: Repeat the concurrency argument at a 60° angle
problems.question: In ABC, A=60°, and the A-bisector, B-median and C-altitude concur. Find C.
problems.idea: The concurrency forces AB=AC.
steps: The bisector-altitude intersection is (b/2,b/(2√3)). On the median from B to the midpoint of AC, the same y-coordinate occurs at fraction 2/3.
Its x-coordinate is c/3+b/6. Setting it equal to b/2 gives c=b.
The triangle is equilateral.

problems.title: An integer root need not exist
problems.question: How many integer solutions satisfy 6x⁵+15x³−18x=171?
problems.idea: Bound the expression at integer inputs.
steps: For x≤−1 the bracket is positive, so the expression is negative; x=0 gives 0 and x=1 gives 3.
For x≥2, the expression is at least its value at 2, namely 276: both x and the positive bracket increase there.
Thus it never equals 171 at an integer.

problems.title: River speed from unequal travel times
problems.question: A boat travels downstream for 2⅓ hours and takes 28 minutes longer to return. Its still-water speed is 16.5 km/h. Find the current speed.
problems.idea: The upstream and downstream distances are equal.
formulas: Down time=7/3 hours; up time=7/3+7/15=14/5 hours.
steps: Let current speed be v. Then (16.5+v)·7/3=(16.5−v)·14/5.
This simplifies to 35(16.5+v)=42(16.5−v), so 77v=7·16.5.

problems.title: A cubic identity when the sum is zero
problems.question: If a+b+c=0, simplify a³+b³+c³.
problems.idea: Use the standard factorization of the sum of cubes minus 3abc.
steps: The first factor is zero, so the whole product vanishes.

problems.title: Exactly twelve trailing zeros in a factorial
problems.question: How many positive integers n make n! end in exactly 12 zeros?
problems.idea: Count factors of 5.
steps: For n=49 the count is 9+1=10; at n=50 it jumps to 10+2=12.
It stays 12 through n=54, then becomes 11+2=13 at n=55.
The valid indices are 50,51,52,53,54.

problems.title: A reciprocal substitution for a system
problems.question: Find x²+y² if 1/(x+y)−1/(y−x)=5/8 and 1/(x−y)−1/(x+y)=3/8.
steps: Solving gives u=1/8,v=1/2.
Thus x+y=8 and x−y=2, giving x=5,y=3.
The denominator restrictions are satisfied.

problems.title: Exterior-angle ratios reverse the order
problems.question: Triangle angles are in ratio 2:3:4. Which listed ratio can describe their three adjacent exterior angles?
problems.idea: Find the interior angles first.
steps: Interior angles are 40°,60°,80°, so the exterior angles are 140°,120°,100°.
In increasing order their ratio is 100:120:140=5:6:7.

problems.title: A point lies on a line
problems.question: For which a does ((a−1)²,3a²) lie on y=3x+9?
problems.idea: Substitute its coordinates.
steps: Expand:3a²=3a²−6a+12.
Thus 6a=12.
